newsitem.title: USA: Key Tech says Q3 hurt by low sales at unit.
newsitem.headline: Key Tech says Q3 hurt by low sales at unit.

text.p: Key Technology Inc, a maker of process automation systems, Friday said its third quarter earnings were hurt by lower sales in one unit and higher-expected-costs for one product.

"Third-quarter operating results were somewhat under our expectation due to lower sales volume in the Automated Inspection Systems business unit (and) higher-than-expected costs to modify Tegra units in the field," Chief Executive Officer Thomas Madsen said in a statement.
Earlier, the company reported a $0.02 per share profit on sales of $13.9 million versus a $0.60 share profit on sales of $17.3 million one year ago.
Financial analysts had forecast earnings between $0.12 and $0.20 a share with the consensus being $0.16 a share, according to First Call.
Key Technology said the low sales in the Automated Inspection unit was due in part to certain customers deferring orders pending results of field upgrades.

Also the company modified some of its previously shipped Tegras systems. Now "substantially completed", the cost of the improvements has been "substantially accounted for in our operating results for the nine-months ended June 30, 1997."
